 Bank of India Star Sunidhi Tax-Saving Deposit: Rates, Lock-In and Tax Treatment 
 By 
 CA Sandeep Kanoi 
 Finance 
 Articles 
 November 21, 2026 
 Share: 
 Summary: Bank of India’s Star Sunidhi is a named tax-saving term deposit for individuals and Hindu undivided families with PAN. The bank states a ₹10,000 minimum, ₹1.5 lakh annual maximum, a tenure from five years up to ten years, no ordinary premature withdrawal or loan facility during the first five years, and normal domestic term-deposit rates . For the five-to-less-than-eight-year retail bucket, the official rate card shows 6.00% for the general public, with the bank’s current additional-rate framework producing 6.75% for senior citizens and 6.90% for super senior citizens on eligible deposits below ₹3 crore. This article explains the product terms, the Income-tax Act, 2025 deduction framework, taxable interest , TDS and DICGC aggregation without recommending the deposit.
 Table of Contents ▸ 
 Star Sunidhi is Bank of India’s named tax-relief term deposit 
 Rate verification for a five-year Star Sunidhi deposit 
 The applicable slab is the normal domestic five-to-less-than-eight-year card rate 
 Senior and super-senior additions depend on age, first-holder status and amount 
 The five-year lock-in changes liquidity and succession planning 
 Tax deduction and interest taxation are separate questions 
 Section 123 and Schedule XV govern the deduction from tax year 2026-27 
 Interest remains taxable and TDS is only a collection mechanism 
 DICGC cover applies at bank level, not certificate level 
 Booking checklist should capture facts that drive rate and tax outcome 
 Frequently Asked Questions on BOI Star Sunidhi 
 What is the official name of Bank of India’s tax-saving FD? 
 What is the minimum and maximum deposit? 
 Can the deposit be closed early by paying a penalty? 
 What rate applies to a five-year deposit? 
 Does the deposit always produce a ₹1.5 lakh tax deduction? 
 Is Star Sunidhi interest tax-free? 
 Is each BOI tax-saver certificate insured up to ₹5 lakh? 
 Key Takeaways 
 Show all 19 sections 
 Advertisement 
 Star Sunidhi is Bank of India’s named tax-relief term deposit
 Bank of India describes BOI Star Sunidhi as its tax-saving deposit scheme. Eligibility is limited to individuals and Hindu undivided families having PAN. The bank publishes a minimum deposit of ₹10,000 and a maximum of ₹1,50,000 per year. Available deposit forms include FDR, monthly-interest, quarterly-interest and double-benefit options, while the selected payout form affects cash-flow timing and compounding rather than the five-year statutory lock-in .
 The published tenure runs from a minimum of five years to a maximum of ten years. A depositor should record the exact contracted maturity because a ten-year certificate is not the same product outcome as a five-year certificate even though both may satisfy the initial lock-in condition. Interest is governed by the normal domestic term-deposit card applicable when the deposit is opened, plus any eligible senior-citizen addition .
 Published feature 
 Bank of India term 
 Practical reading 
 Eligible depositor 
 Individual or HUF with PAN 
 Confirm PAN and first-holder eligibility before opening 
 Deposit amount 
 Minimum ₹10,000; maximum ₹1,50,000 per year 
 The product cap also aligns with the aggregate section 123 ceiling , but other eligible payments share that ceiling 
 Tenure 
 Five years to ten years 
 Record the selected maturity; five years is the minimum, not the only tenure 
 Premature withdrawal 
 Not permitted up to five years, except death-related payment under applicable rules 
 Do not treat an ordinary FD breakage penalty as an available exit 
 Advance against deposit 
 Not available for five years from deposit date 
 The certificate cannot be assumed available as collateral during lock-in 
 Rate verification for a five-year Star Sunidhi deposit
 The applicable slab is the normal domestic five-to-less-than-eight-year card rate
 Star Sunidhi does not publish a separate promotional yield. It takes the normal domestic term-deposit rate for the selected maturity. Bank of India’s official rate page, checked on 21 November 2026, shows 6.00% per annum for callable domestic deposits below ₹3 crore in the five-years-to-less-than-eight-years bucket. The 2 November 2026 revision changed selected medium-term buckets; the five-year retail bucket remained at 6.00% in the current card information.
 Senior and super-senior additions depend on age, first-holder status and amount
 For eligible retail deposits below ₹3 crore with a tenure of three years or more and up to ten years, the bank states an additional 0.75 percentage point for senior citizens and 0.90 percentage point for super senior citizens. Applied to the 6.00% base, the five-year rates are 6.75% and 6.90% respectively. The bank defines senior citizen as age 60 or above but below 80, and super senior citizen as age 80 or above. Eligibility should be confirmed at booking, especially for joint accounts and HUF deposits.
 Depositor category 
 Five-year bucket rate checked 21 Nov 2026 
 Qualification 
 General public 
 6.00% p.a. 
 Retail callable domestic term deposit below ₹3 crore 
 Senior citizen 
 6.75% p.a. 
 Eligible first holder, age 60 to below 80; 0.75% additional rate for 3–10 years 
 Super senior citizen 
 6.90% p.a. 
 Eligible first holder, age 80 or above; 0.90% additional rate for 3–10 years 
 The five-year lock-in changes liquidity and succession planning
 Ordinary premature withdrawal is not permitted during the first five years. That is a product and tax-saver feature, not merely a penalty choice. The depositor should therefore keep emergency liquidity outside Star Sunidhi and should not assume that paying a lower interest rate will unlock the certificate. The bank also states that an advance facility is unavailable for five years and that the term deposit cannot be pledged as security for another advance.
 The bank provides a death exception : where the depositor dies before maturity, the nominee or legal heir may receive premature payment even within the lock-in subject to applicable rules, and the premature-payment penalty is exempted. Nomination is available generally, but the product page states that no nomination shall be made for a term deposit applied for and held by or on behalf of a minor. Depositors should obtain the bank’s current operating documents for the precise survivor, nominee and claim process.
 Tax deduction and interest taxation are separate questions
 Section 123 and Schedule XV govern the deduction from tax year 2026-27
 For deposits made on or after 1 April 2026, the current statutory reference is section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 read with Schedule XV . It allows an individual or HUF a deduction for enumerated eligible payments and deposits within an aggregate ceiling of ₹1,50,000 for the tax year, subject to the Schedule conditions. Star Sunidhi’s bank product page still uses the familiar section 80C label, but current-year tax work should map the deposit to the 2025 Act rather than cite the repealed numbering mechanically.
 The ₹1,50,000 is an aggregate deduction ceiling, not a separate allowance for this FD. Life-insurance premium , provident-fund contributions and other qualifying items can consume the same limit. Further, deductions under section 123 are not available where the individual’s total income is computed under the concessional regime in section 202 , subject to the Act’s terms. A deposit may therefore satisfy product eligibility while producing no incremental deduction for a particular taxpayer.
 Interest remains taxable and TDS is only a collection mechanism
 Tax-saving status does not exempt the interest. Interest is included in income under the applicable method and head, and the bank applies TDS rules to the customer’s aggregate interest with the bank rather than assessing each certificate in isolation. For the current 2025 Act framework, the threshold commonly relevant to bank time-deposit interest is ₹50,000 for other depositors and ₹1,00,000 for senior citizens, subject to section 393 , current rules, PAN and any valid declaration. No TDS does not mean no tax; the depositor must report taxable interest even where withholding is nil.
 DICGC cover applies at bank level, not certificate level
 Bank of India is a bank deposit-taker, so eligible fixed deposits fall within the DICGC framework . The insurance limit is ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank in the same right and same capacity , inclusive of principal and accrued interest. All eligible deposits at different branches of Bank of India are aggregated. Opening several Star Sunidhi certificates or using multiple BOI branches does not create a separate ₹5 lakh cover for each certificate.
 Different ownership capacities can be treated separately only under DICGC’s rules; labels should not be engineered without genuine legal capacity. The insurance limit is not a guarantee of timely liquidity, a return guarantee beyond covered deposits, or a reason to ignore nomination and records. Depositors should preserve deposit receipts, PAN, joint-holder mandate and nomination acknowledgement so the bank can identify the correct depositor capacity.
 Booking checklist should capture facts that drive rate and tax outcome
 Before booking 
 Evidence to retain 
 Why it matters 
 Product and tenure 
 Star Sunidhi application and deposit receipt 
 Confirms tax-saver product and exact maturity 
 Rate and age benefit 
 Rate-card snapshot, date of booking and age/first-holder proof 
 Supports the contracted general, senior or super-senior rate 
 Tax deduction 
 Tax regime choice and schedule of all section 123 payments 
 Prevents double counting of the ₹1.5 lakh aggregate ceiling 
 Interest and TDS 
 Interest certificate, Form 26AS/AIS and bank TDS record 
 Reconciles taxable interest and credit for withholding 
 Deposit insurance capacity 
 List of BOI deposits in the same right and capacity

 Frequently Asked Questions on BOI Star Sunidhi
 What is the official name of Bank of India’s tax-saving FD?
 Bank of India identifies the product as the BOI Star Sunidhi Deposit Scheme or Star Sunidhi Tax Saving Deposit Scheme.
 What is the minimum and maximum deposit?
 The bank publishes a ₹10,000 minimum and a ₹1,50,000 annual maximum for Star Sunidhi.
 Can the deposit be closed early by paying a penalty?
 Ordinary premature withdrawal is not permitted during the first five years. Death-related payment may be allowed under the bank’s applicable rules.
 What rate applies to a five-year deposit?
 The official card places five years to less than eight years at 6.00% for general retail deposits below ₹3 crore, with eligible additions resulting in 6.75% for senior and 6.90% for super-senior citizens.
 Does the deposit always produce a ₹1.5 lakh tax deduction?
 No. The ceiling is aggregate across eligible section 123 items, and the taxpayer’s chosen tax regime and other conditions determine actual deduction.
 Is Star Sunidhi interest tax-free?
 No. Interest remains taxable. TDS, where applicable, is withholding and does not determine the final tax liability.
 Is each BOI tax-saver certificate insured up to ₹5 lakh?
 No. DICGC aggregates eligible deposits across all BOI branches for the same depositor in the same right and capacity, including principal and interest.
 Key Takeaways
 Star Sunidhi is a genuine Bank of India tax-saving term deposit for eligible individuals and HUFs with PAN.
 The published amount range is ₹10,000 to ₹1,50,000 per year, with a five-to-ten-year tenure.
 The five-year bucket is 6.00% for general customers, 6.75% for eligible senior citizens and 6.90% for eligible super senior citizens based on the current card framework.
 No ordinary premature withdrawal, loan or pledge is available during the first five years; death claims follow special rules.
 The deduction is governed by section 123 and Schedule XV of the 2025 Act, while interest remains taxable and DICGC cover is aggregated per depositor per bank.
 *****
 Disclaimer: This article is an educational review of Bank of India’s BOI Star Sunidhi Deposit Scheme, its official domestic term-deposit rate page, the Income-tax Act, 2025 and DICGC information accessed and checked on 21 November 2026. It is not a recommendation, ranking, return forecast, solicitation, tax opinion or substitute for the bank’s current application form, deposit receipt, branch confirmation, statutory text or professional advice. Interest rates can change without notice and the contracted rate depends on the booking date, maturity, amount, age, first-holder status, customer category and bank verification. The article explains the five-year retail bucket and published additional-rate framework but cannot confirm a future booking or resolve an inconsistency between a product page and the live rate card. Tax deduction depends on the taxpayer’s regime, aggregate eligible payments, ownership and compliance with Schedule XV; interest remains taxable even where TDS is not deducted. DICGC insurance is subject to its law, eligible-deposit rules and aggregation by depositor, bank, right and capacity, and is not equivalent to unlimited principal protection or immediate liquidity. Depositors should verify current official terms with Bank of India and obtain individual tax and legal advice before opening, renewing, nominating, assigning income or acting on a death claim.
